rationale: The actual human review here was light (approved, four nitpick-style comments about moving helpers to utils, an all2all-kwargs style question, and whether a patch.py hunk was rebase-relevant); neither candidate hits any of these, so recall is low for both. Both independently converge on the same deep bug (num_stale_output_tokens double-seeding on the replace_streaming_prompt path) and the Qwen2.5-Omni registry regression, cross-validating those findings for both. Y backs nearly every claim with quoted line-level evidence and explicitly hedges uncertain claims (e.g. flags the ming_flash_omni.py concern as 'unproven; not filed'), while X asserts an unverified 'CI gates are red' claim with no evidence trail and a likely-incorrect claim that generation-stage randomize_inputs ignores its own kwarg (contradicted by Y's more internally-consistent reading), denting X's precision. X is the more polished, human-readable review with concrete proposed code diffs, giving it a slight actionability edge, but Y's stricter evidence discipline makes it the more trustworthy review overall.
